observations: Photo 0: Black DSLR body with 'Nikon' logo on front, mounted with a long zoom lens, sitting on a seller-branded 'McSteve' box.
Photo 1: Top-down view of the lens barrel showing engraved markings 'Nikon', 'DX', and focal markings 70-100-135-200-300, consistent with a 70-300mm zoom lens.
Photo 2: Side view of the camera body showing visible wear, scuffing and discoloration on the grip/rubber area near the lens mount.
No shot shows the rear LCD screen, a power-on state, a shutter-count display, or any engraved model number (e.g. 'D3400') on the body itself.
Box shown is a reseller's generic branded box ('McSteve Online Gadget Store'), not original Nikon packaging, so it proves nothing about authenticity or completeness.
No accessories (battery, charger, strap tag, memory card, caps) are clearly shown aside from the body and lens.

identity.kind: DSLR camera with telephoto zoom lens

claims.claim: This is a Nikon D3400 DSLR Camera
claims.evidence: Nikon brand is visible on the body (photo 0), but no model number 'D3400' is legible in any photo; body design is consistent with several similar entry-level Nikon DSLRs.
Lens barrel in photo 1 shows '70-300mm' and 'DX' markings consistent with a Nikon AF-P 70-300mm lens.

claims.claim: Working perfectly ok with no fault
claims.evidence: No photo shows the camera powered on, a working LCD, shutter firing, or autofocus/zoom in action; condition of sensor, shutter count, and electronics cannot be assessed from stills.

risks.risk: Camera body may not be a D3400 or may be a different/lower-spec model misrepresented by the seller.
risks.proof: A clear photo or screen capture of the camera's info/menu screen showing the model name, or a label/sticker on the body/battery door showing the model number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unidentified entry-level Nikon DSLR body rather than specifically a D3400

risks.risk: Electronic/mechanical function (shutter, sensor, autofocus, LCD) may be faulty despite 'working perfectly' claim.
risks.proof: A short video clip showing power-on, LCD display active, shutter firing, and lens autofocus/zoom in action.

risks.risk: Visible wear/scuffing on the grip (photo 2) could indicate heavy use or even prior drop damage affecting internal alignment.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all sides of the body, especially corners and mount, plus a photo of the lens mount for signs of impact.

risks.risk: Lens glass/elements may have fungus, scratches, or focus issues not visible in the current photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of front and rear lens elements against a light source, and a photo through the viewfinder showing a clear image.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lens condition unknown/worst case (possible optical fault)

risks.risk: Unknown shutter actuation count, which heavily affects DSLR resale value.
risks.proof: A photo of the shutter count from the camera's info screen or EXIF data from a fresh test shot.

risks.risk: Missing or unconfirmed accessories (battery, charger, memory card, strap, caps) that are usually part of a full kit.
risks.proof: A single photo showing all included accessories laid out together.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body + lens only, no accessories

proof_requests: Photo of the camera powered on, showing the model name on the LCD or info screen.
Photo/video of the shutter count display (via menu or software).
Video clip showing power-on, autofocus, zoom, and shutter firing.
Close-up photos of the lens front/rear elements against light.
Close-up photos of all body corners and the lens mount for dents or impact marks.
Photo of all included accessories (battery, charger, caps, strap, memory card) laid out together.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Nikon DSLR body with a 70-300mm zoom lens, so it can be priced at worst case given the unverified 'D3400' model claim, unverified functional condition, and visible body wear.
